Malay Mail KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 9 — Forget saving space in your suitcase for that next Seoul shopping spree. Some of South Korea's coolest fashion and beauty labels are bringing the goods straight to Malaysia.
 From minimalist wardrobe staples and cult handbags to perfumes that double as art objects, a fresh wave of Korean brands have made its way into Malaysian malls in 2026, with more arrivals on the horizon.
 Here are the names worth knowing.
 The wardrobe refresh 
 South Korean casualwear label TOPTEN10 made its Malaysian debut at Sunway Pyramid in January, followed by a second outlet at 1 Utama in July.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Think relaxed silhouettes, fuss-free basics and easy layering pieces that would look right at home in a K-drama airport scene.
 Founded in 2012, the brand offers an affordable alternative for shoppers who prefer understated everyday fashion without the flashy logos.
 And it has company on the way.
 Musinsa Standard, the in-house label of South Korean fashion platform Musinsa, is preparing to enter Malaysia after securing an exclusive distribution agreement with retail group Mitra Adiperkasa (MAP) in August.
 Known for its contemporary essentials and minimalist streetwear, the label plans to open stores in Kuala Lumpur and other major Malaysian cities, although dates and locations have yet to be announced.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The expansion follows impressive online demand from Malaysian shoppers, with Musinsa reporting average annual transaction volume growth of 63 per cent between 2023 and 2025 on its global store, followed by a 117 per cent year-on-year surge in the first half of 2026.
 Clearly, Malaysians have been doing their Korean fashion homework.
 The bag obsession 
 If your social media feed has been serving up effortlessly cool Korean handbags, chances are Stand Oil has made an appearance.
 Founded in Seoul in 2018, the accessories label has built a following with its sleek shoulder bags, retro-inspired shapes and playful proportions.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Its appeal lies in handbags that feel both practical and fashion-forward, with enough personality to make even a basic jeans-and-T-shirt combination look intentional.
 And there is no need to order from overseas. Stand Oil now has a boutique on Level 4 of Pavilion Kuala Lumpur, allowing shoppers to check out the bags in person.
 The beauty takeover 
 No Korean shopping story would be complete without K-beauty, and Malaysia's skincare obsession shows little sign of slowing down.
 Among the latest arrivals is Shinsegae Hyperground, the South Korean retail giant's pop-up platform, which has opened at Seibu in The Exchange TRX.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Running until March 2027, the space will feature a rotating selection of more than 10 Korean fashion and beauty labels, including Dinto, Headspa7, Fivebybe, Marie Claire and Tansanmagnesium.
 Meanwhile, Malaysian beauty retailer HERMO has returned to bricks-and-mortar shopping with a store at The Campus in Ampang, bringing together Korean skincare and cosmetics in a space designed for browsing and discovering new products.
 There is also Olive Young, the Korean beauty powerhouse that has become practically compulsory on Seoul shopping itineraries.
 Rather than opening a standalone Malaysian store, the retailer has partnered with Sephora to bring a curated selection of Korean beauty brands to local shoppers, with a dedicated discovery space launched at Fahrenheit88 in September.
 Smells like Seoul 
 The next name to watch is Tamburins, the cult Korean fragrance and beauty label from the company behind eyewear brand Gentle Monster.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Known for sculptural perfume bottles, unconventional fragrances and stores that resemble contemporary art galleries, Tamburins has made beauty products feel like fashion accessories.
 Its celebrity connections have only added to the hype, with campaigns featuring Blackpink's Jennie, Stray Kids' Felix and actor Byeon Woo-seok.
 The label is preparing to open its first Malaysian boutique at Suria KLCC, although an official opening date has yet to be announced.
